questions.question: Q1. Which formula is correctly used in the simulation to compute the Coupling Efficiency (eta) based on alignment offset (x) and air gap (z)?

explanations.a: This option incorrectly models the alignment offset as a linear decay factor instead of a squared exponential drop-off.
explanations.b: Correct. The simulation engine calculates coupling efficiency using a peak baseline of 90% multiplied by exponential decay factors for the squared alignment offset and vertical air gap.
explanations.c: This option mistakes the transmission power limit of 120 kW for the maximum coupling efficiency baseline of 90%.
explanations.d: While this represents the relationship between power and efficiency, it is not the structural equation used to compute efficiency from the physical coordinates.

questions.question: Q2. What is the constant nominal power transmitted (P_transmitted) by each active road coil segment in this laboratory setup?

explanations.a: 90.0% represents the maximum calibrated coupling efficiency under ideal positioning alignment, not the track power capacity.
explanations.b: This is an arbitrary baseline value that does not match the transmitter specs configured in the source engine.
explanations.c: Correct. The embedded track charging segments are designed to deliver a constant high-frequency power of 120.0 kW.
explanations.d: 1000.0 kJ represents the total storage capacity of the target vehicle battery pack, not the transmission power rate.

questions.question: Q3. According to the laboratory framework, a vehicle with an air-gap distance of z = 24.5 cm falls under which silhouette profile?

explanations.a: The Sedan profile is strictly bounded between a low clearance range of 5.0 cm and 13.0 cm.
explanations.b: The Crossover SUV profile captures intermediate vehicles with clearances spanning 13.0 cm to 20.0 cm.
explanations.c: Correct. Any vertical clearance tracking greater than 20.0 cm up to the 30.0 cm maximum limit triggers the high-clearance Delivery Van profile.
explanations.d: This category is completely outside the scope of the three primary profiles established in this laboratory framework.

questions.question: Q4. How does the continuous integration function track accumulated battery energy gain (Delta E) over active charging zones?

answers.a: By integrating vehicle speed over the total session duration
answers.b: By taking the direct product of maximum coupling efficiency and elapsed time
answers.c: By integrating the varying instantaneous power received over exposure time
answers.d: By dividing the current state of charge by the baseline transmission factor

explanations.a: Integrating speed determines the total spatial distance covered, not the electrochemical energy captured by the battery circuit.
explanations.b: Efficiency alone does not translate to accumulated energy without considering power integration timelines.
explanations.c: Correct. Active energy integration is calculated mathematically as the definite time integral of the instantaneous received power across dynamic exposure cycles.
explanations.d: This formulation yields an incorrect parameter dimension that violates standard power conversion laws.

questions.question: Q5. What physical behavior is represented by the lane alignment index crosshair on the top-down radar display?

answers.a: The instantaneous vehicle transit velocity scaled by coil spacing
answers.b: The manual calibration adjustment of the lateral alignment offset value
answers.c: The mechanical oscillation frequency of the wishbone suspension links
answers.d: The automatic thermal protection trip boundary condition

explanations.a: Transit velocity governs the speed of road scrolling animation, not the coordinate shifting on the lane index crosshair.
explanations.b: Correct. The radar inset crosshair serves as a tracking interface mapping the alignment offset (x) relative to the center track limits.
explanations.c: The suspension link lines connect structural anchors in the side profile canvas but are not mapped onto the top-down lane radar.
explanations.d: Thermal conditions are absent from this experiment's engine, which focuses solely on geometric alignment and electromagnetic decay links.
